en: The Collection of Threes, Chapter on the Inner Circle.
3. The Vaḍḍhakīsūkarajātaka “Excellent, excellent! You have wandered about seeking slaughter in the past, having overcome the pigs in this place.”
"So now you sit meditating alone, having gone apart;
O tiger, does your strength not fail you today?
"These [beasts] indeed used to go in every direction before," he replied.
Many people, overcome by fear and seeking refuge,
now dwell together in one place,
where they are difficult for me to subdue.
Having seen this for myself, I declare it a marvel:
that where tusked tigers have conquered the deer."
"Through harmony, one is released from the power of the teeth.
Thus ends the third Jātaka, the Vaḍḍhakīsūkarajātaka.
